title: BMN Spread Complexity Across Phase Transitions
abstract: We investigate the dynamical behavior and spread complexity of quantum states within the mass-deformed BMN matrix model equipped with an emergent $U(1)$ global charge at finite temperature $β^{-1}$ and chemical potential $ν$. Focusing on the strong-coupling regime ($μ\gg 1$), we model the dynamics via a charged Thermofield Double (cTFD) state and trace the evolution of spread complexity across three distinct thermodynamic regimes. In the low-temperature gapped phase ($βμ\gg 1$), discrete mass-gap bound states dominate, trapping wavepacket dispersion and producing non-chaotic, oscillatory early-time growth. Conversely, in the high-temperature continuum phase ($βμ\ll 1$), thermal excitations overwhelm the mass gap, driving a transition to a continuous advection field that exhibits maximal chaotic scrambling with a Krylov Lyapunov exponent $λ_K = π/ β$ that saturates the universal bound. In the intermediate temperature regime ($βμ\sim 1, βν\sim 1$), the interplay between mass-gap bound states and the continuous thermal background induces a sub-leading correction to the Lanczos coefficients $b_n \sim \fracπβ n + γ\sqrt{n}$, governing a continuous sub-exponential crossover before full chaotic thermalization. Technical derivations regarding KMS boundary conditions, grand canonical spectral moments, residue analysis, and time-reversal symmetry breaking in Krylov space are detailed in four dedicated appendices.
summary: This paper analyzes how the complexity of quantum states evolves in the BMN matrix model as it passes through different thermal phases. By modeling the system using a charged Thermofield Double state, the authors predict distinct dynamical signatures—from oscillatory behavior to maximal chaos—depending on the temperature and mass gap scales. This provides a detailed theoretical map of quantum thermalization in this specific strongly coupled gauge theory context.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamical behavior and spread complexity of quantum states across different thermodynamic regimes in the BMN matrix model.
main_result: The complexity exhibits distinct behaviors depending on the temperature regime: non-chaotic oscillation in the low-temperature gapped phase, maximal chaotic scrambling in the high-temperature continuum phase, and a sub-exponential crossover in the intermediate regime.
method: The analysis employs the charged Thermofield Double (cTFD) state formalism and utilizes diagnostics like spread complexity, Krylov Lyapunov exponents, and the analysis of Lanczos coefficients.
model_or_system: The system is the mass-deformed BMN matrix model equipped with an emergent U(1) global charge, studied at finite temperature (beta^-1) and chemical potential (nu).
key_observables: Spread complexity C(t), Krylov Lyapunov exponent (λ_K), and Lanczos coefficients (b_n).
important_parameters: Temperature (β^-1), chemical potential (ν), and the mass deformation parameter (μ), analyzed across regimes defined by their relative scales (e.g., βμ >> 1, βμ << 1).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using the charged Thermofield Double (cTFD) state, and the analysis relies on detailed spectral moment calculations and boundary condition assumptions.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the framework in the strong-coupling limit, then detailing the distinct physical regimes (low-T gapped, high-T continuum, intermediate crossover) and the mathematical tools required for each.
why_interesting: The study of complexity measures across phase transitions is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in strongly coupled quantum systems, bridging concepts from quantum chaos and thermalization.
